subject: Throughput sizing: tokens/sec, QPS & peak vs steady-state (FinEx)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finex.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Throughput sizing: tokens/sec, QPS & peak vs steady-state (FinEx)

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the productive discovery call earlier. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so we can size a realistic throughput profile for your pilot: 

Summary of FinEx workload (as we captured):
- Primary use: transaction summarization + compliance highlight extraction for customer support chat.
- Typical request: ~1200 tokens in, ~200 tokens out (average).
- Real-time constraint: streaming preferred for the chat UI (partial tokens to the client).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 600ms for first token, end-to-end for short responses <= 1.5s.
- Concurrency: baseline 50 concurrent streams during business hours, peak up to 350 concurrent during batch processing windows.
- Traffic profile: steady-state QPS ~8–12 req/s; short 10–15 minute bursts where QPS jumps to ~60–80, occasionally to ~120 for a 30–60s spike.

Next steps I promised:
1) Please share a sample CSV of minute-level queries or a few representative days of traffic (timestamps, tokens per request, streaming yes/no).
2) Confirm if any requests require long-context (>32k tokens) or persistent session KV cache.
3) I'll loop in Marissa (solutions) and Neha (infrastructure) to provide a preliminary throughput/instance sizing and an options matrix (hosted vs Dedicated) by EOD Thursday.

Attaching our template for sample traffic and a small throughput worksheet (see attachments). If you can drop the CSV into the Drive link we shared, we’ll ingest it for a quick estimate.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: finex-throughput-sample-traffic.csv (csv stub), redwood-prelim-sizing.xlsx (xls stub)

From: Alice Park <alice.park@finex.com>

Cc: ops@finex.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing: tokens/sec, QPS & peak vs steady-state (FinEx)

Thanks, Rafael — great recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 1200 tokens in is the long-tail; median is closer to 600 tokens in and 150 out.
- Streaming is required for the chat UI (we want first-token RTT to render progressively); the compliance extraction can be non-streaming async.
- We do not have >32k contexts in pilot; some enterprise customers may require 64k later but not now.
- Concurrency numbers: baseline 50 concurrent chat sessions at any given minute, but our peak pattern is more like a gradual ramp to 300 over 10 minutes (during market opens) and then a 90s microburst reaching ~420 QPS-equivalent for API-backed batch jobs.
- We also evaluate cost: if Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost by >=25% we'll lean that direction.

I uploaded two days of minute-level traffic to the Drive folder and included an Ops contact in CC who can share additional logs if needed.

Alice Park
Head of Engineering, FinEx Corp
alice.park@finex.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing: tokens/sec, QPS & peak vs steady-state (FinEx)

Appreciate the upload and clarifications, Alice. We pulled the two days and did an initial pass — see notes below and attached preliminary sizing workbook.

Quick observations (based on the sample CSV):
- Median tokens/request: 620 in / 140 out. Mean ~780/165 (long tail skew).
- Minute-level steady-state: 10 req/s (avg), 12 req/s (p95).
- Verified pattern: ramp to ~300 concurrent over 10 minutes, microbursts to ~420 QPS-equivalent for short windows (60–120s).

Sizing implications / options:
1) Hosted (multi-tenant) pilot:
   - To meet 95th-first-token <= 600ms with streaming for chat, we recommend a mix of 2x high-throughput GPU instances behind a smart router with prefix caching; this covers steady-state and short burst handling with autoscaling buffer.
   - Estimated sustained token/sec capacity: ~45k tokens/sec across the pool (assumes quantized model, 8-bit where appropriate).
   - Expected 95th latency: 400–550ms first-token at steady-state; spikes may hit 700–900ms during the 420 QPS microbursts without aggressive pre-warming.

2) Dedicated pool (reserved capacity):
   - For predictable microburst handling and a ~25% lower per-token unit cost at your volumes, a Dedicated cluster (3x performance-optimized nodes) is recommended.
   - Estimated sustained token/sec: ~120k tokens/sec for the cluster, headroom for QPS spikes with autoscale/burst credit.
   - Can meet 95th-first-token < 500ms consistently with streaming enabled and warm KV caches.

Actions we recommend to finalize sizing:
- Confirm model choice (we provided suggestions on the call; model family impacts kernel selection and tokens/sec).
- Provide representative 1-week traffic (minute granularity) if possible.
- Quick sync: 30-min call tomorrow for Marissa to run the workbook live and lock numbers.

Marissa and Neha — can you take a look at the attached workbook and propose a Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation we can send to Alice with ballpark cost?

Thanks — Rafael

Attachments: redwood-prelim-sizing.xlsx (updated)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Throughput sizing: tokens/sec, QPS & peak vs steady-state (FinEx)

Thanks Rafael — jumping in with a quick preliminary sizing note from Solutions/Infra: 

Prelim Dedicated recommendation (pilot -> production ramp plan):
- Pilot (4 weeks): 2x p4d-equivalent instances (reserved short-term) plus 1x burst node; this supports streaming for chat and gives ~40–50k tokens/sec of effective throughput with room to increase concurrency via batching tweaks.
- Prod baseline (after pilot): 3x performance nodes + 2x burst nodes (autoscale to 5); estimated sustained ~110k tokens/sec, headroom for 420 QPS spikes with warm caches.

Key questions for FinEx to confirm for final quote:
- Final model selection (latency vs quality tradeoffs).
- Whether you want per-tenant KV-caches persisted (adds ~10–15% memory footprint).
- Any compliance constraints that require Private deployment rather than Dedicated (will affect procurement).

I’ll prepare a one-pager with cost ranges (hosted vs Dedicated) and send by EOD. In the meantime, Rafael — happy to run a live walkthrough of the sizing sheet on the sync.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
